diagnostics.message:
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
aws_cloudtrail.main depends on aws_s3_bucket.cloudtrail (via s3_bucket_name) but not on aws_s3_bucket_policy.cloudtrail, which grants cloudtrail.amazonaws.com s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:PutObject on the bucket. CloudTrail validates bucket write access when the trail is created and starts logging, so if the trail is applied before the bucket policy, creation fails (InsufficientS3BucketPolicyException) or early log deliveries are dropped. The bucket policy is a separate resource with no ordering edge to the trail, so an explicit depends_on is required (this matches the pattern in the official aws_cloudtrail documentation example).

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
`aws_cloudtrail.main` depends only on the S3 bucket itself, not on `aws_s3_bucket_policy.cloudtrail`. CloudTrail validates the bucket policy granting `cloudtrail.amazonaws.com` the `s3:GetBucketAcl`/`s3:PutObject` permissions when the trail is created/updated; if the policy is not yet applied, trail creation can fail or the trail will be created but will be unable to deliver logs (AWS may stop logging within hours). The official `aws_cloudtrail` documentation explicitly shows `depends_on = [aws_s3_bucket_policy.example]` in its reference example. There is no attribute on the trail that can reference the bucket policy, so a bare `depends_on` is the right fix.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
aws_cloudtrail.main references the CloudTrail log bucket via s3_bucket_name = aws_s3_bucket.cloudtrail.id, but nothing orders it after aws_s3_bucket_policy.cloudtrail. CloudTrail validates that the bucket's policy grants cloudtrail.amazonaws.com s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:PutObject when the trail is created; if the trail is applied before the bucket policy, creation fails with InsufficientS3BucketPolicyException. The official aws_cloudtrail documentation shows depends_on = [aws_s3_bucket_policy.example] for exactly this reason, and this project's bucket policy lives in a separate resource with no attribute link to the trail.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
module.eventbridge's rule targets reference aws_sns_topic.security_alerts arn, which orders the module after the SNS topic, but nothing orders it after aws_sns_topic_policy.security_alerts. The topic policy is what grants events.amazonaws.com permission to sns:Publish; if the EventBridge targets are created before the policy is applied, event deliveries to the topic fail until the policy exists. An explicit depends_on from module.eventbridge on the topic policy ensures the policy is in place before alerts start flowing.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
`module.eventbridge` creates EventBridge rules whose targets publish to `aws_sns_topic.security_alerts` (referenced via the topic ARN), but it has no dependency on `aws_sns_topic_policy.security_alerts`. The topic policy granting `events.amazonaws.com` permission to publish (`Allow_Publish_Events`) is what actually authorizes EventBridge deliveries; if the policy is applied after the rules/targets, events fired in that window are dropped. There is no attribute on the module that could reference the topic policy, so a bare `depends_on` is the right fix.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
module.eventbridge creates EventBridge rules whose targets publish to aws_sns_topic.security_alerts[count.index].arn (implicit dependency on the topic exists), but it has no ordering against aws_sns_topic_policy.security_alerts. The topic's default policy does not grant events.amazonaws.com permission to publish; that grant only exists once aws_sns_topic_policy.security_alerts is applied. If the rules are created before the policy, every event delivered to the SNS target is rejected until the policy lands, silently dropping all security-alert notifications. A bare depends_on is the appropriate fix here, since there is no natural attribute of the policy to reference from the module.
